result.summary: RECONSTRUCTED HANDOFF -- written 2026-09-03 after the fact; timestamps are reconstructed approximations. Independently confirmed at reconstruction time: (1) :service_task_ssrf_validation_enabled's default is true (Application.get_env(:letflow, :service_task_ssrf_validation_enabled, true), read directly in http_transport/3's body) -- an absent config value is the safe (validation ON) value, matching Letflow.Webhooks's identical :webhook_ssrf_validation_enabled convention exactly. (2) Grepped config/dev.exs and config/prod.exs for service_task_ssrf_validation_enabled: zero matches in either -- the flag is never overridden to false outside test config, so production and dev environments both get real SSRF validation on every dispatch. Confirmed config/test.exs does NOT set this flag to false either (grepped directly) -- the run's own tests rely on the injectable-resolver 4-arity http_transport/4 clause or a real local test server, not on a blanket test-config bypass, which is the stricter and safer of the two mechanisms available (matching this backfill's own reading of Letflow.Webhooks's own precedent, which likewise defaults to per-test injection over a blanket config flip where practical). (3) Confirmed exactly one :httpc.request/4 call site still exists in the whole module (grep -c ':httpc.request' lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher.ex, inside do_http_transport/3 only) -- the 3-arity/4-arity http_transport split adds a resolver parameter, it does not add a second HTTP call site. (4) :catalog_service fix re-verified structurally complete: traced the 3-clause case match in do_attempt_dispatch/2 directly -- :inline_url is the ONLY clause reaching http_transport/3; :catalog_service and the malformed-snapshot clause both terminate at handle_failure/4 without ever constructing an HTTP request. (5) Tenant isolation: claim_due_dispatch_ids/2 and attempt_dispatch/2 both still take tenant_schema as an explicit parameter and thread it through every Repo call with prefix: tenant_schema (re-confirmed by reading both functions directly) -- no change to this pattern from rework2. Overall PASS -- no new confidentiality, injection, or cross-tenant issue found; the new test seam is safely non-reachable in any real environment.
